questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass from the lane with the broken line. You cannot pass from the lane with the solid line.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you better, even if they don't help you see much farther.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after you stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you must stop. You cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. Wait for a green signal before you go.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots, even with mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.

questions.question: How should you park on a hill?

options.text: One rear wheel should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it when facing downhill, or gently touch it when facing uphill.

questions.question: When parking uphill with no curb, after setting the parking brake, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the edge of the road.
Turn them away from the edge of the road.
Keep them facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels right toward the edge. This makes the vehicle roll away from the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What are bicycles considered when used on roadways?

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving in two directions.

questions.question: When a green arrow appears with a red light, when can you turn in that direction?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
Wait until the light changes.
If you are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear. Always yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Sound a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to step in front of your vehicle. This can warn them of danger.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no one can cross them to pass from either direction.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it off the main road completely if you can.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up entering curves and slow down leaving them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking on a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: The correct way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal your intention. Slow down and stay in the right lane as close to the right curb as possible.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination quickly.
Turn up your radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you are struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Stop and rest.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Are in blind spots or too close for the truck driver to stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to travel safely behind the truck.
Are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in blind spots or too close for the truck driver to stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or maneuver safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Never pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parked facing uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This lets other drivers, motorcycle riders, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you intend to do.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns allowed.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs warn drivers of a no passing zone.

questions.question: When should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Bad weather makes it hard for other drivers to see your car. Headlights make your vehicle more visible. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: It is very foggy. You should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let traffic on the main road go first when you merge.
Always stop completely.
Use your turn signal and enter traffic at normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let traffic on the main road go first when you merge.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means you must let other vehicles pass before you proceed. You do not have to stop if no cars are coming, but always slow down and enter carefully.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them with one outside mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check them by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots, and other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road changes direction or becomes narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road changes direction or becomes narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves or gets narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or before narrow bridges.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Use cruise control safely.
Make speed and direction changes slowly and smoothly.
Drive the same way you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change your speed and direction gradually. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may slip and you could lose control of your vehicle.
